back: Government measures that restrict trade, usually by limiting imports or helping local producers, to protect domestic industries.
Specific: a fixed amount per unit. Ad valorem: a percentage of the value of the import.
A legal limit on the quantity (or value) of a good that can be imported in a period.
Selling goods abroad at a price below their cost of production (or below the home price).

front: Tariff versus quota: which raises revenue?
back: A tariff raises revenue; a quota does not (unless import licences are sold).
Infant industries, declining industries, strategic industries, anti-dumping, current account deficit, revenue, demerit goods/environment, jobs.
Higher prices and less choice; inefficiency of protected firms; dearer inputs for other firms; retaliation; lost gains from trade.

front: Effect of a tariff on price, local output, imports and consumers?
back: Price rises; local output rises; imports fall; consumers pay more and buy less; the government gains revenue.
Government limits on the foreign currency residents may buy, which restrict their ability to import.
